title: Introduce 'Quant Sentinel': telemetry-driven FP8 gating and staged fallback for H100 E4M3/E5M2
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Deploy a telemetry-driven gating layer ("Quant Sentinel") that can safely enable FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) profiles on H100 deployments by combining fine-grained probes, rolling healthchecks, and deterministic rollback triggers. The sentinel should allow progressive activation across shards and tenants, surface per-layer quality regressions, and orchestrate automatic fallback to safe profiles (INT8/FP16) when SLOs or accuracy thresholds are breached. This ticket focuses on the runtime gate + orchestration pieces, probe signal design, and operational runbook; separate tickets will handle calibration model artifacts and data capture pipelines.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Quant Sentinel exposes a runtime gate that can be toggled per-cluster and per-shard and accepts a probe policy configuration.
2) Telemetry signals (latency P95, token-error-rate, perplexity delta on golden prompts, per-layer activation drift) are ingested to the sentinel and evaluated against configured thresholds.
3) Sentinel can execute staged rollouts: shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 100% with automated hold/rollback decisions.
4) Automated fallback executes within configured SLO window and emits a rollback event with root-cause summary.
5) Dashboards: rollout status, probe pass/fail, and historical probe traces available in Console.
6) Runbook documented with play-by-play for manual override, emergency rollback, and postmortem template.
implementation_notes: High-level approach: add a gating microservice (stateless controller) that subscribes to probe telemetry topics and maintains per-deployment state. Probe suite will include: (a) golden prompt accuracy checks using a small diverse prompt set; (b) synthetic stress prompts for long context KV/caching behavior; (c) latency/throughput probes at varying batch sizes to expose scheduling regressions. Use existing telemetry pipeline (metrics + traces) and add a lightweight aggregator that computes rolling windows and anomaly scores. Integrate with rollout manager to apply progressive activation and to trigger fallback actions. Fallback options: static profile swap to INT8, immediate FP16 failover, or divert to dedicated capacity pool. Ensure all decisions are idempotent and recorded to the audit log.
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for gate logic, threshold evaluation, and state transitions.
2) Integration test that replays synthetic telemetry to validate staged activation and rollback.
3) Canary: enable on non-prod H100 pool with canary traffic and shadow profile for 48h.
4) Golden-run validation comparing output distributions (n-gram overlap, token-level KL) on holdout set before and after activation.
5) Chaos: simulate RPC drops and partial shard failures to validate idempotent rollback behavior.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: False positives from noisy telemetry causing unnecessary rollback. Mitigation: smoothing windows, majority voting across probes, and minimum-duration holds before rollback.
Risk: Rollback latency causing user-facing errors if fallback warms slowly. Mitigation: pre-warm INT8/FP16 pool and employ fast path API switch.
Risk: Observability blindspots for per-layer FP8 activation. Mitigation: add per-layer counters and sample gradients into debug bucket for failed probes.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: RFC drafted; Quant Sentinel name and scope agreed in weekly infra sync.
2025-02-18: Probe signal matrix defined; golden prompt seed set curated (150 prompts across conversational, code, and retrieval).
2025-02-24: Initial gate prototype implemented; exposes API to set policy and query status. Local unit tests passing.
2025-03-01: Telemetry aggregator integrated; can compute rolling anomaly score from synthetic probes. First end-to-end staging run scheduled.
2025-03-02: Design review with PM (Jia Huang) and Design (Emilie Tran) — feedback: add UI affordances for manual hold and an explainability field in rollback events. Action items created.
review_feedback: PM Jia Huang: emphasize customer-facing SLA behavior and ensure default policy is conservative for standard customers.
Design Emilie Tran: Console UX must show probe payloads and sample generation snippets to aid debugging.
SRE Marcus Liu: require an explicit quorum-based decision for cross-region rollouts to avoid split-brain decisions.
next_steps:
1) Implement pre-warm flow for fallback profiles and add warmness metric.
2) Wire explainability field into audit logs and expose in Console.
3) Complete canary in staging cluster and collect 72h of probe traces.
4) Schedule a customer-impact review before enabling for any production tenant.
